problem: If $\,u(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{7t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,v(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]\,$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$, find $Aw(t)$ where $w(t)=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{7t} \\ 3{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}].$

feedback.problem: If $\,u(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,v(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}]\,$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$, find $Aw(t)$ where $w(t)=[\begin{aligned}-2{e}^{-t} \\ -{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $u(t)$ and $v(t)$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ the superposition principle guarantees that 

$$
cu(t)+dv(t)
$$

 is also a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for all $c,d\in R.$

Notice that 

$$
w(t)=-2u(t)-v(t).
$$

 

Therefore, $w$ is a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$ So, in order to find $Aw(t)$ we just need to find ${w}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Aw & ={w}^{′}(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(-2{e}^{-t})^{′} \\ (-{e}^{t})^{′}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-t} \\ -{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
